Ingest mission and program text

Source: R/md-ingest-orgtext.R
md_ingest_orgtext.Rd

Fills orgtext, the last empty core table: one row per (ein, tax_year, text_kind) carrying what an organisation wrote about what it does.

Usage

md_ingest_orgtext(version = "v2_2", con = NULL, kinds = NULL)

Arguments

version

Pinned efile_orgtext version.

con

A connection from md_db().

kinds

Which text kinds to load. Defaults to all present.

Value

Row counts by kind, invisibly.

It is adjudication input, not candidate generation

Section 10 is explicit that this stays outside the name and address selection machinery. pf_purpose_tiebreak() consumes mission text after a candidate list exists, to choose between candidates that already look plausible. It is not a blocking key and must not become one - at four million EINs and paragraph-length strings, blocking on it would be a disaster.

So orgtext is deliberately EIN-keyed and joined on demand. It carries no variant_class, appears in no spec axis, and nothing in md_compile() will ever select on it.

Why it is a panel and the other tables are not

name and address collapse repeated observations into one row per distinct value, because a spelling written twice is not two spellings. Text is different: an organisation rewrites its mission, and the rewrite is a fact about that year rather than a duplicate to be merged. Rows are therefore kept per (ein, tax_year, text_kind), and identical text repeated across years is preserved rather than deduplicated.

Text is stored as filed

No case folding, no punctuation stripping, no truncation. The normalised forms that name carries exist because names are matched on; mission text is read, quoted and shown to an adjudicator, so mangling it would destroy the thing that makes it useful. Any normalisation a consumer wants is a consumer's decision.
